executive_summary:
Your amber status is entirely supplier-driven, centered on geopolitical concentration rather than demand or macro weakness. Four critical chokepoints dominate: China-exposed EMS and battery suppliers (Smoore, Huizhou BYD, EVE Energy) face overlapping US-China trade and Taiwan contingency risks; printing substrate sources (Stora Enso, IP Sun, Sappi) are scattered across NATO borders, US-China friction, and African infrastructure stress respectively; and nicotine sourcing from India (ITC, high exposure) adds South Asian geopolitical tail risk. Texas Instruments' unexplained 2.4% stock decline warrants a quick call to confirm no hidden supply or demand signal, but this reads as secondary noise versus the concentrated China bet across EMS and batteries.

The urgent play: map dual-source alternatives for EMS and battery components within 30 days—current suppliers represent critical BAT exposure in the highest-tension theater. Stora Enso and ITC can wait for quarterly review unless new sanctions materialize. Sappi's energy crisis is a 60-day operational watch, not an immediate redesign trigger.
